abstract: Sample mispairs are common and potentially costly mistakes, and therefore checking for sample mispairing is a crucial quality-control step in multimodal genomic studies. This study presents an independent benchmark of sample mispairing detection tools in multimodal transcriptomic cancer datasets. In pseudobulk experiments with known sample pairings, four tools achieved near-perfect F1 scores across datasets. In real-data experiments, three tools performed particularly well, and sample mispairs were identified in three of five datasets. Finally, a high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma dataset is reconstructed: resolving mispairs between two bulk RNA-sequencing modalities, resolving mispairs between pooled single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data, and reestablishing the connection between the transcriptomic data and patient metadata using genetic ancestry inference.
